threshold: Mapped DNR parking asset within 100 meters of a DNR named recreation trail reference, plus independently named park access on official map or park guide. Not independently ground-checked.

points.title: Lake of the Clouds overlook parking
points.summary: At the end of M-107, a short overlook approach leads toward a remarkable sight: Lake of the Clouds resting below the escarpment. This DNR-mapped lot is near the ridge-trail area, but the easy overlook walk and strenuous Escarpment Trail are very different adventures.
points.visitorAdvice: If you are towing a camper or trailer, the DNR directs visitors to a separate staging area near the ski hill in busy seasons. We have not verified that staging lot's exact navigation point.
points.coordinatesPurpose: DNR mapped parking asset; no claim of vacancy, open gate, plowed lot, or precise pedestrian entrance

points.title: Summit Peak approach parking
points.summary: Here the forest walk is part of the reward. Leave the mapped Summit Peak area and follow the signed woodland approach toward a tower that rises above the hardwood canopy. The DNR describes roughly a half-mile walk before the stairs.
points.visitorAdvice: The DNR directs campers and trailers to a separate lower staging area near the South Boundary Road turnoff. We have not verified an exact navigation point for that staging area.
points.coordinatesPurpose: DNR mapped parking asset; no claim of vacancy, open gate, plowed lot, or precise pedestrian entrance

points.title: Presque Isle River trail-area parking
points.summary: The Presque Isle River makes itself known through the sound of falling water and the dark rock of the gorge. This DNR-mapped river-trail parking area is a place to orient yourself before choosing the signed path toward Nawadaha, Manido or Manabezho.
points.visitorAdvice: The DNR identifies a shorter approach to Nawadaha from behind the Presque Isle contact booth. This particular asset has not been matched to that exact entrance or to every waterfall platform.
points.coordinatesPurpose: DNR mapped parking asset; no claim of vacancy, open gate, plowed lot, or precise pedestrian entrance

points.title: Pinkerton Trailhead parking
points.summary: Beyond the roadside overlooks lies another Porkies experience: long forest paths and quiet backcountry. This mapped parking point aligns with the Pinkerton Trail, where a wilderness walk needs a deliberate plan.
points.visitorAdvice: Use the official DNR trail map for the whole hike, including creek crossings, distance and the walk back. This map pin does not certify a safe crossing or an open route.
points.coordinatesPurpose: DNR mapped parking asset; no claim of vacancy, open gate, plowed lot, or precise pedestrian entrance

points.title: Visitor Center Nature Trail parking
points.summary: Near the park's eastern entrance, begin by noticing the forest itself. The Visitor Center Nature Trail area offers an introduction to the northern woods and the stories behind the landscape, when seasonal services and trails are available.
points.visitorAdvice: Check visitor center hours with the park before planning an indoor stop. The mapped parking asset is not an assurance that the building or trail is currently open.
points.coordinatesPurpose: DNR mapped parking asset; no claim of vacancy, open gate, plowed lot, or precise pedestrian entrance

points.title: Winter sports trail-area parking
points.summary: When winter settles over the eastern ridges, the Porkies can be a place of snow-covered trees and quiet trail corridors. This mapped parking area is near the DNR winter-sports trail network.
points.visitorAdvice: Before traveling, consult the Ski the Porkies trail and snow report. An official mapped lot does not guarantee open lifts, groomed tracks, chalet services or plowed parking.
points.coordinatesPurpose: DNR mapped parking asset; no claim of vacancy, open gate, plowed lot, or precise pedestrian entrance
